name: AI 3D Model Generation
summary: Multi-provider AI 3D model generation supporting text-to-3D and image-to-3D workflows with glTF/USD export. Primary provider is Kie with fallback support for alternative services, generating production-ready 3D meshes with textures and materials in 15-45 seconds.

inputs.description: Optional reference image for image-to-3D conversion. Provides visual guidance for shape, color, material properties, and overall composition. Critical for converting photographs or artwork into 3D models.

Text prompt describing the desired 3D object or scene. Can include geometry details, material properties, artistic style, level of detail, and use-case context (e.g., 'game asset', 'product visualization', 'architectural element').

outputs.description: 3D model URL pointing to glTF (.glb/.gltf) or USD format file. Includes embedded or referenced textures, materials, and PBR properties for real-time or offline rendering.
3D model metadata including format (glTF/USD), vertex count, texture resolution, bounding box dimensions, material count, generation time, and provider details for asset management.

executionNotes: This node interfaces with Kie as the primary 3D generation provider, supporting both text-to-3D and image-to-3D conditioning. The selectedModel field is required and routes to appropriate provider. Parameters like polygon_budget (high-poly for render, low-poly for real-time), material_quality (PBR, diffuse, specular), and export_format (glTF binary, glTF+separate textures, USD) are dynamically exposed via inputSchema per model. Outputs are saved to savedFilePath with sanitized savedFilename. Bounding box and vertex count enable downstream LOD (level-of-detail) optimization. Typical generation latency: 15-45 seconds depending on complexity and desired fidelity. Models support immediate import into Three.js, Babylon.js, or professional 3D tools.

exampleConnections.scenario: Photo-to-3D modeling: Convert product photographs, architectural sketches, or concept art into production-ready 3D models for visualization or gaming.
2D-to-3D conversion pipeline: Generate a 2D image first, then convert to 3D for multi-modal content creation (e.g., concept art → game asset).
Direct 3D generation: Create 3D objects from pure text descriptions for rapid prototyping and visualization tasks.
Prompt engineering for 3D: Use LLM to refine vague concepts into detailed 3D specifications (e.g., 'sculpture of a dragon' → detailed geometric and material properties).
3D rendering to video: Render 3D model from multiple angles or with animation, then pipe to video generation for dynamic marketing or AR preview content.
